title: De Silva, Kamindu fifties guide Sri Lanka to 221-4 in first Test
text:

Sri Lanka's Dhananjaya de Silva (R) and Kusal Mendis (L) run between the wickets during the third day of the first Test (Aamir QURESHI) Fifties from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis helped Sri Lanka reach 221-4 at lunch on day three of the opening Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi on Wednesday.
 After resuming at 114-3, De Silva was on 87 after reaching his 21st half-century, while skipper Kusal Mendis was 21 not out, leaving the tourists still 213 runs behind Pakistan's first innings 434-9 declared.
 Sri Lanka lost just one wicket in the session as De Silva and Kamindu put on a 91 for the fourth wicket, enjoying a stroke of fortune along the way.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement De Silva, on 38, flashed at a Razaullah delivery but Saud Shakeel failed to hold on a sharp chance at slip.
 De Silva took full advantage of the reprieve and has so far hit nine fours off 121 balls.
 Kamindu completed his eighth Test fifty before edging Mohammad Abbas to wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori to leave Sri Lanka 155-4.
 Kamindu's 58 came off 131 balls 58 with eight fours.
 Seamer Abbas (2-33) was the pick of the Pakistan bowlers while fellow quick Saqib Khan has taken 2-82 on his debut.
